methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $117M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
VEIR, a Series B climate and energy company founded by Tim Heidel that has raised $117M to date, is valued using two primary methods triangulated against a peer set of 9 private and 1 public comparable company in the frontier energy sector.

Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x multiplier to the $117M total raised proxy, yielding $222M. This reflects typical valuation step-ups from Series B to subsequent funding rounds. Peer-median analysis draws on three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B, Series C), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B, Series C), and Amogy ($700M, Series C)—generating a median valuation of $1.0B with a range of $700M to $3.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects heterogeneous risk profiles and development stages within early-stage climate tech.

Triangulation of these two methods supports a valuation range of $189M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $611M. The substantial spread reflects material uncertainty around VEIR's capital efficiency, technology de-risking trajectory, and addressable market capture relative to peers. Stage-progression anchors the downside; peer benchmarking anchors the upside. Key uncertainties include competitive positioning within the peer cohort and the extent to which VEIR's development progress justifies a premium or discount to median peer valuations at Series B.
